executiveSummary: A benefit-dinner talk for Ridley Smiles: a dental van that parks at rural schools reaches children a clinic never sees, and $250 keeps one child out of pain for a year.

slides.subtitle: Spring benefit dinner · Ridley County
slides.speakerNotes:
- Good evening, and thank you for coming out on a school night.
- I want to tell you about Jamie, and about a van.

keyBullets: 1 in 3 children in Ridley County have never seen a dentist
Source: county health survey, 2023
slides.speakerNotes:
- One child in three in this county has never sat in a dentist's chair.
- Jamie was one of them. She was eight when her teacher noticed she was eating lunch on one side of her mouth.
slides.intent: Make the scale and the child real

keyBullets: Nearest pediatric clinic: 40 miles
No bus route to it
A visit costs a parent a day's pay
slides.speakerNotes:
- Jamie's mom works the line at the poultry plant. The nearest clinic that takes children is forty miles away, and there is no bus.
- Going means a day without pay. So, like a lot of parents here, she waited.

keyBullets: A fully equipped dental van
Parks at the school one day a month
A child misses one class, not one day
slides.speakerNotes:
- So we brought the dentist to the school. The van has two chairs, an X-ray, and a hygienist and a dentist.
- Jamie walked out of math class, across the parking lot, and was back before lunch.

keyBullets: Parents sign one form at the start of the year
The school nurse makes the list
Cleanings, sealants, and fillings on board
Anything bigger goes to a partner clinic, with a ride
slides.speakerNotes:
- Parents sign one form in August, and the school nurse does the rest.
- Most of what children need we do on the van. For anything bigger, we book a partner clinic and send a ride.

keyBullets: 1,180 children seen in two years
Untreated decay among them fell from 41% to 19%
slides.speakerNotes:
- In two years the van has seen eleven hundred and eighty children at six schools.
- When they first came on board, forty-one percent had a cavity no one had treated. A year later it was nineteen.

keyBullets: “She eats on both sides now. She smiles in pictures.”
Jamie's mother
slides.speakerNotes:
- Jamie had three fillings and two sealants on the van.
- Her mom wrote us a note. I keep it on my desk.

keyBullets: Same day, every month
slides.speakerNotes:
- The one thing that made the biggest difference was boring: the same day every month.
- When families know the van comes on the second Tuesday, nine children in ten come back for their follow-up.

keyBullets: $250 keeps one child out of pain for a year
$3,000 covers a school for a month
Three schools are on the waiting list
slides.speakerNotes:
- Two hundred and fifty dollars covers one child for a year: the visits, the fillings, and the ride if they need it.
- Three more schools have asked for the van. Tonight, we'd like to say yes to them.

slides.slideTitle: One van, one school day, one child out of pain
slides.subtitle: Give tonight at the tables
keyBullets: $250 keeps a child like Jamie out of pain for a year
slides.speakerNotes:
- A clinic forty miles away never saw Jamie. A van in her school parking lot did.
- Two hundred and fifty dollars does that for one more child this year. Thank you.
